name: shadetree-ai-plugins
description: Claude plugins for consulting client automations, each bundling a local FastMCP server (and Skills) as a one-command install.

plugins.name: iphone
plugins.description: Read (and send) iMessage history, read Mac/iPhone call history (cellular + FaceTime), and look up Contacts — all locally on this Mac. macOS only; requires Full Disk Access.

plugins.name: career-navigator
plugins.description: Conversational career exploration for a high school student: infers a RIASEC (Holland Code) profile through natural conversation, then matches it against a local O*NET occupational dataset. Fully local — no accounts, no hosting, no network calls at runtime.

plugins.name: claude-usage-analyzer
plugins.description: Analyzes local Claude Desktop/Cowork usage plus an optional claude.ai account export, and produces a live, self-updating HTML dashboard covering a workspace reorganization (which chats belong in which Projects, each Project's name/description/custom instructions, and file structure), a usage & best-practices review (project/chat counts, model-usage breakdown, chats that used an overly complex model, and recommended public skills/plugins/connectors vs. custom ones worth building), and a workspace checkup that audits your standing custom instructions for bloat and duplication. Built for business users of the Claude Desktop app; Claude Code CLI sessions are deliberately excluded. Read-only analysis; never moves, renames, or deletes anything on its own.

plugins.name: grilling
plugins.description: Stress-tests a plan, decision, or idea by interviewing you relentlessly: walks the decision tree one question at a time through the structured question tool, leads every question with a recommended answer, looks up anything discoverable instead of asking, and withholds any action until you confirm shared understanding. Based on Matt Pocock's grill-me skill.

plugins.name: handoff
plugins.description: Compacts the current conversation into a portable handoff document a fresh agent can pick up: writes it to the OS temp directory with a timestamped name, references specs and diffs by path instead of copying them, redacts secrets, and names the skills the next agent should reach for. Also lists the handoffs on disk and resumes one straight back into the work. Based on Matt Pocock's handoff skill.
